metadata.title: AASLD Practice Guidance on Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis and Cholangiocarcinoma
metadata.source: American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases (AASLD)
metadata.scope: Diagnosis, management, and surveillance of primary sclerosing cholangitis and cholangiocarcinoma

definition.description: Chronic cholestatic liver disease characterized by inflammation, fibrosis, and stricturing of intrahepatic and/or extrahepatic bile ducts

variants.variant: Classic form with strictures visible on cholangiography
Features of both PSC and autoimmune hepatitis
Important differential diagnosis; responds to corticosteroids

epidemiology.ibd-association: 60-80% have concurrent inflammatory bowel disease (usually ulcerative colitis)

laboratory.finding: Elevated bilirubin (late finding or suggests dominant stricture)
ANA and SMA may be positive

findings.finding: Multifocal strictures with intervening dilations (beaded appearance)

histology.indication: Not required for diagnosis in typical cases
Helpful when small duct PSC suspected

guidance-statements.statement: PSC should be suspected in patients with cholestatic liver biochemistries, particularly those with IBD
MRCP is the preferred initial imaging modality for diagnosis
IgG4 levels should be checked to exclude IgG4-related sclerosing cholangitis
Liver biopsy is not required for diagnosis in classic large duct PSC

mre.advantage: Less affected by inflammation than TE

model.name: Amsterdam-Oxford
model.variables: Age, bilirubin, albumin, platelets, AST, years since diagnosis

model.name: UK-PSC Risk Score
model.variables: Age, bilirubin, albumin, platelets, alkaline phosphatase

drug.name: Ursodeoxycholic acid (UDCA)
drug.evidence: Improves biochemistry; no proven survival benefit in randomised trials
drug.caution: High doses (28-30 mg/kg/day) associated with worse outcomes

medical-therapy.guidance-statement: UDCA at moderate doses may be considered but is not routinely recommended

dominant-stricture-management.definition: Stricture >1.5 mm in common bile duct or >1 mm in hepatic duct

approach.step: Cytology and/or biopsies to exclude CCA

dominant-stricture-management.guidance-statement: Dominant strictures should be sampled to exclude CCA

condition.name: Inflammatory bowel disease
condition.recommendation: All PSC patients should undergo colonoscopy at diagnosis
condition.surveillance: Annual colonoscopy with biopsies for colorectal cancer surveillance

polyp-management.recommendation: Cholecystectomy for any gallbladder mass or polyp in PSC
polyp-management.rationale: High risk of malignancy in PSC patients

condition.name: Fat-soluble vitamin deficiency
condition.recommendation: Monitor and supplement vitamins A, D, E, K as needed

risk-in-psc.peak-risk: Within first year of PSC diagnosis and at time of decompensation

surveillance.recommendation: Annual surveillance with MRI/MRCP and CA 19-9

imaging-findings-concerning-for-cca.finding: Progression of stricture on serial imaging
Biliary dilation proximal to stricture with progressive worsening

limitations.limitation: Lewis antigen negative patients (5-10% of population) do not produce CA 19-9
Elevated in cholangitis, cholestasis, other malignancies

fish-for-polysomy.description: Fluorescence in situ hybridisation for chromosomal polysomy

diagnostic-workup.guidance-statement: Multimodal approach often needed; negative cytology does not exclude CCA

type.name: Perihilar cholangiocarcinoma (pCCA)
type.location: Between second-order bile ducts and cystic duct insertion

risk-factors.factor: Leading risk factor in Western countries
Endemic in Southeast Asia (Opisthorchis viverrini, Clonorchis sinensis)

molecular-alterations.guidance-statement: Comprehensive genomic profiling recommended for advanced CCA

surgical-resection.indication: Localised disease amenable to complete resection

by-location.pcca: Hepatectomy with bile duct resection; may require vascular resection

liver-transplantation-for-pcca.protocol: Mayo protocol (neoadjuvant chemoradiation followed by LT)

criteria.criterion: Unresectable pCCA or pCCA arising in PSC
No prior attempt at surgical resection

section.name: PSC Diagnosis
section.statement: Suspect PSC in patients with cholestatic liver tests, particularly with IBD
Check IgG4 to exclude IgG4-related disease
Liver biopsy not required for classic large duct PSC

section.name: PSC Management
section.statement: UDCA at moderate doses (13-23 mg/kg/day) may be considered
Manage dominant strictures with ERCP and tissue sampling

section.name: Cancer Surveillance
section.statement: Annual MRI/MRCP and CA 19-9 for CCA surveillance
Annual colonoscopy for colorectal cancer surveillance in PSC-IBD
Cholecystectomy for any gallbladder polyp in PSC

section.name: CCA Diagnosis
section.statement: Multimodal diagnostic approach for suspected CCA
Negative cytology does not exclude CCA
Consider FISH for polysomy in indeterminate strictures

section.name: CCA Treatment
section.statement: Surgical resection for localised resectable disease
Liver transplantation under strict protocols for selected pCCA
Comprehensive genomic profiling for advanced disease
